# Project Angerona (AngeronaSuite) - llms.txt

Version: 1.10.2
Date: 2026-08-25
License: MIT
Repository: https://github.com/Ag3nt47/AngeronaSuite

## LATEST (v1.10.2 - governed autonomous defense and final improvement loop)

- Adversary Combat performs typed, exact-target local containment under signed
  response contracts. Actions use fsynced intents, an HMAC hash-chain journal,
  verified postconditions, exact Undo, idempotency, crash recovery, and a
  mutation circuit breaker.
- SOAR and manual response surfaces delegate to Combat and reconcile signed
  receipts. SUBMITTED is not VERIFIED. Queue IDs and exact target identities are
  bound to the action lifecycle.
- ARIA requires typed keyboard confirmation for consequential actions. Voice,
  gesture, callbacks, model output, and retrieved content cannot confirm writes.
- The governed `aria-defense-llama3` pack verifies exact manifest and Ollama blob
  identities before activation. Knowledge packs are inert; no downloaded
  executable skill or runtime installer is accepted.
- Ollama calls re-attest the loopback listener, process birth, executable path
  and signature, fixed route, no-proxy/no-redirect policy, and response bounds.
- Sysmon covers event IDs 1-29 and 255 with an HMAC-authenticated cursor.
  Community ID v1 and OCSF 1.8 provide cross-sensor identity and data mapping.
- Source Sandbox is confined and inert. Fleet credentials are finite and
  secrets remain in protected custody.
- Final validation: 1,255 pytest passed, 3 intentional skips, 0 failed from
  1,258 cases across 197 files; compile 308/308; Ruff/import/discovery/duplicate
  gates passed; 46 module, 20 core/Shark, and 15 ARIA self-tests passed; direct
  and batch selfcheck passed 26/26; pip-audit found no known vulnerabilities.
- Combat validation: 128/128 negative controls. Live winning round: 52/52
  detection, 52/52 response, 13/13 contracts, 13/13 verified closure,
  resilience PASS, zero active reversible records/rules/probes after cleanup,
  and intact signed journal.
- Red-team verdict: no open Critical, High, or Medium release blocker. One
  non-blocking defense-in-depth Medium remains: retained OS process handle plus
  bounded executable-file identity lease for path-wide program firewall rules.

## Product contract

Angerona is a local-first EDR/NDR/SOAR and DFIR workbench with safe MITRE ATT&CK
validation and a local Ollama assistant. It is intended for home labs,
defensive research, purple-team practice, learning, and portfolio use.

It is not an independently certified commercial EDR/XDR product and does not
claim complete attack coverage, commercial fleet parity, or external efficacy
validation.

## Platform contract

- Windows: Protect. Full supported user-mode telemetry and governed response;
  elevation is required for the complete path. No unsigned kernel driver ships.
- macOS: Observe preview. Privacy-minimized process/flow observation and shared
  core. No Endpoint Security or Network Extension enforcement claim.
- Linux: Observe plus optional BCC/eBPF. Rootless process/flow/posture visibility;
  privileged kernel telemetry is an explicit supplement.

## Architecture

- `src/angerona/core/`: EventBus, storage, response contracts, ARIA/runbook RAG,
  model packs, OCSF/Community ID, policy, credentials, secure stores, cases,
  evidence, interoperability, and platform abstractions.
- `src/angerona/modules/`: independent `BaseModule` detectors and responders.
  Current frozen discovery: 67 modules, no duplicate names or codes.
- `src/angerona/gui/`: Classic dashboard, Flow Dashboard / Local SOC, Settings,
  operations, Scan Center, Red Team, ATT&CK, Adversary Combat history/Undo, and
  Upgrade Console.
- `src/angerona/shark/`: non-destructive attack simulation and AAR generation.
- `src/angerona/telemetry/`: bounded process/network snapshots and normalized
  sensor data.
- `tools/`: compile, selfcheck, release, validation, and owner-verified helper
  commands.
- `analysis/loop/`: red-team, remediation, performance, innovation, and final
  verification evidence.

Normal flow:

sensor/module -> typed Event -> HMAC EventBus -> recorder/correlation ->
incident/SOAR -> signed response contract -> Adversary Combat -> durable intent
-> exact action -> verified postcondition -> signed receipt -> Undo/recovery

## Response authority

Adversary Combat is the governed mutation boundary. A response request names
only allowed action types and exact identities. Process actions bind PID,
creation time, and executable. Network actions bind literal peer data and/or an
exact executable. File actions bind exact validated paths. Host isolation is a
separate explicit escalation authority and is not inherited from ordinary weak
signals.

Supported governed response classes include:

- block exact remote peer;
- isolate exact executable/program;
- suspend or terminate verified process;
- quarantine exact file, including verified cross-volume copy/delete and Undo;
- activate bounded deception/honeypot response;
- isolate host under explicit typed escalation policy;
- undo one or all verified reversible actions.

Protected/system targets, stale process identities, path replacement, ambiguous
PowerShell semantics, weak cross-entity correlation, and unsigned or malformed
contracts fail closed.

## Detection and evidence

- Windows: ETW, WMI/CIM, AMSI, WFP, Defender, Security log, Sysmon EIDs 1-29+255.
- Detections: process lineage, persistence, file integrity, memory injection,
  LSASS access, shadow-copy tamper, ransomware, C2 cadence, USB, BYOVD posture,
  deception, YARA/YARA-X, network novelty and peer behavior.
- Correlation: Evidence Lattice, Telemetry Expectation Contracts, incidents,
  ATT&CK mapping, Community ID v1, OCSF 1.8, Suricata/Zeek import, guarded
  osquery snapshots.
- Evidence integrity: HMAC-signed events and cursors; Combat uses a durable HMAC
  hash-chain journal with legacy unsigned records distinguished from current
  signed records.

## ARIA and model packs

- Local Ollama is the default AI path; optional cloud/provider paths require
  separate explicit consent and protected credentials.
- ARIA tools are typed and registered. Arbitrary shell is not a tool.
- Consequential confirmation is accepted only from exact typed keyboard input.
- Retrieved documents, emails, pages, voice, gestures, model output, and callback
  text are untrusted evidence, not control authority.
- `aria-defense-llama3` is an approved local model pack with exact manifest/blob
  checks. Install/activate/rollback/remove operations are bounded and serialized.
- Source Sandbox stages inert artifacts. Runtime installers, executable skills,
  symlinks/reparse escapes, and arbitrary GitHub code imports are refused.

## Operator surfaces

Canonical menu/info sections are Help, Dashboard, Settings, Operations,
ATT&CK Map, Red Team, and Advanced Console. High-value destinations include:

- Live Alerts, Resolve Center, SOAR Queue, Scan Center, Top Talkers;
- Flow Dashboard / Local SOC: Overview, Cases, Hunt, Assets, Detection Content,
  Parity & Interop, Audit;
- Settings: General, System, Enterprise, ARIA, Trusted Processes, Mobile, API Keys;
- ATT&CK: Live Heat, Coverage, Top Techniques;
- Red Team: Run, History, Device Security Lab, Sandbox Editor;
- Advanced Console: Mobile, AI Sandbox & Models, Watchdog, Telemetry;
- Host Adaption: audit, baseline, drift, preview, sandbox, apply, rollback,
  automation, feedback, and activity;
- Adversary Combat: policy, mode, action history, verified-only filters, Undo
  selected, Undo all, recovery state, and maximum validation.

## Data and secrets

Windows packaged data prefers protected `D:\AngeronaData`, with protected
`%ProgramData%\Angerona` fallback. Source/development uses the configured data
root. macOS uses the application-support area. Linux uses XDG state.

Secrets use Windows DPAPI, macOS Keychain, or Linux Secret Service. Plaintext
fallback is not accepted when the protected backend is required. Runtime data,
credentials, diagnostics, journals, models, evidence, and local state are not
source artifacts and must not be committed.

## Build, run, and validation

Windows source:

    Install-Angerona.bat
    start-angerona.bat

Development:

    python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
    python -m pytest -q
    python -m ruff check src tests tools
    python tools/compile_check.py
    python tools/selfcheck.py
    run-selfcheck.bat
    python run_aria_selftests.py
    run-adversary-combat-validation.bat

The Combat validation batch is intentionally defensive. It uses bounded local
probes, verifies responses and cleanup, and must not be expanded into exploit,
credential, persistence, remote scanning, or hack-back behavior.

## Measured performance evidence

- Runbook RAG: 25.5x real-index speedup; 4.38x synthetic corpus speedup.
- ETW PID cache: 92.2% lower peak tracked allocation in a 100,000-PID stress.
- Upgrade Console: about 0.036 ms Qt submission for a simulated 50 ms read;
  single-flight coalescing prevents timer backlog.
- Literal loopback validation: 2.16x faster while hostname resolution and
  listener/process/path attestation remain in force.
- Ransomware same-directory normalization: 6.91x faster on the 100,000-record
  correlation benchmark.
- Network novelty expiry: 1.88x faster in the no-expiry 20,000-entry state case.

## Known limits and backlog

Shipped claims must remain distinct from proposals. Current proposals include:

- retained OS process handle and bounded executable-file identity lease for
  program-wide firewall actions (open defense-in-depth item R6-03);
- signed segmented Combat journal after forged-prefix and crash-rotation proof;
- OS-native listener-bound Ollama owner proof before reducing call-time checks;
- strict signed Sigma 2.1 correlation runtime;
- YARA-X cost admission and hot-rule rollback;
- journal-backed ransomware/deception attribution;
- bounded STIX/TAXII lifecycle;
- signed Linux CO-RE sensor sidecar;
- constant-time first-run Sysmon seek and asynchronous initial ARIA index build.

External acceptance remains for long elevated soak, physical sleep/resume,
clean-machine install/upgrade/uninstall, publisher signing/notarization, native
Linux/macOS release execution, fleet-scale throughput, false-positive baselines,
and independent defensive efficacy testing.

## Explicit non-goals

- offensive payloads, exploit creation, credential theft, evasion, remote
  scanning, attack infrastructure, hack-back, or persistence;
- arbitrary shell/script response or model-authored host mutation;
- downloaded executable skills, unverified models, insecure Ollama pulls, or
  bulk unreviewed community artifacts;
- unsigned kernel drivers or unsupported claims of ETW-TI protected-process
  access;
- automatic weakening of security policy, GPO/MDM reversal, log clearing, or
  permanent broad containment without explicit retained policy.
